1444843.name: Redmond
1444843.original: So named because of red-colored mounds west of the town.
1444843.rewrite: Named for the red mounds west of the town.

1444889.name: Richfield
1444889.original: Vacated 1867 because of Indian troubles, resettled 1870. So named because of the richness of the soil. First called Omni for a Book of Mormon character.
1444889.rewrite: Settlers left in 1867 because of conflicts with Native Americans and returned in 1870. Named for the richness of the soil. First called Omni for a Book of Mormon character.

1444892.name: Richmond
1444892.original: There are two theories as to the origin of this name: 1. That it was named for Charles Coulson Rich, early settler and Mormon Church official. 2. That it was so named because of the rich loamy soil.
1444892.rewrite: Two theories exist about the name: one holds that it was named for Charles Coulson Rich, an early settler and a leader in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints; the other, that it was named for the rich, loamy soil.

1444992.name: Riverdale
1444992.original: Outgrowth of Ogden. So named because of its proximity to Weber River. Formerly called Stringtown because the first houses were built principally along a single road in a long "string" extending southeast from Ogden. First called Jack Thompson's Settlement, for John C. Thompson, early settler. Also temporarily called Union.
1444992.rewrite: An outgrowth of Ogden. Named for its proximity to the Weber River. Formerly called Stringtown because the first houses were built mainly along a single road in a long "string" extending southeast from Ogden. First called Jack Thompson's Settlement, for John C. Thompson, an early settler. Also temporarily called Union.

1445146.name: Rosette
1445146.original: So named because of the abundance of wild roses in this vicinity.
1445146.rewrite: Named for the abundance of wild roses in the area.

1445262.name: Salem
1445262.original: Named for Salem (Jerusalem) Palestine. First called Pond Town because of a large natural pond near the settlement.
1445262.rewrite: Named for Salem (Jerusalem), Palestine. First called Pond Town because of a large natural pond near the settlement.

1445269.name: Salina
1445269.original: Vacated 1866 because of Indian troubles, resettled 1871. Derived its name from Salina Creek, which received its name from the Spanish word meaning salt, because of the large deposits of rock salt in the vicinity.
1445269.rewrite: Settlers left in 1866 because of conflicts with Native Americans and returned in 1871. Named for Salina Creek, whose name comes from the Spanish word meaning salt, because of the large deposits of rock salt nearby.

1445329.name: Santaquin
1445329.original: Named for a Ute Indian leader. Formerly called Summit Creek, taking the name of the stream that flows through the settlement.
1445329.rewrite: Named for a Ute leader. Formerly called Summit Creek, after the stream that flows through the settlement.

1445376.name: Scipio
1445376.original: Named for a famous Roman warrior, at the suggestion of Brigham Young. First called Round Valley, because it is situated in a circular-shaped valley.
1445376.rewrite: Named for a famous Roman warrior, at the suggestion of Brigham Young. First called Round Valley because it sits in a circular valley.

1445380.name: Scofield
1445380.original: Named for General Charles W. Scofield.
1445380.rewrite: Named for Gen. Charles W. Scofield.

1445446.name: Sevier
1445446.original: So called because it is situated on the Sevier River and at the mouth of Sevier Canyon.
1445446.rewrite: Named for its location on the Sevier River at the mouth of Sevier Canyon.

1445583.name: Sigurd
1445583.original: Outgrowth of Vermilion. Origin of name unknown.
1445583.rewrite: An outgrowth of Vermilion. Origin of name unknown.

1445709.name: Smithfield
1445709.original: Named for John G. Smith, early settler.
1445709.rewrite: Named for John G. Smith, an early settler.

1445755.name: Snyderville
1445755.original: Named for G. G. Snyder, who shipped the first ore from the Park City mining district.
1445755.rewrite: Named for G. G. Snyder, who shipped the first ore from the Park City mining district.

1445910.name: South Ogden
1445910.original: Outgrowth of Ogden. So named because it is south of Ogden. Formerly called Burch Creek for a pioneer family which settled here in 1848.
1445910.rewrite: An outgrowth of Ogden. Named for its location south of Ogden. Formerly called Burch Creek for a pioneer family that settled here in 1848.

1445935.name: South Weber
1445935.original: So named because it is on the south side of the Weber River.
1445935.rewrite: Named for its location on the south side of the Weber River.

1445945.name: Spanish Fork
1445945.original: Derived its name from Spanish Fork Creek, which was so named because the Old Spanish Trail followed by Father Escalante in 1776 closely paralleled it.
1445945.rewrite: Named for Spanish Fork Creek, which got its name because the Old Spanish Trail followed by Father Escalante in 1776 closely paralleled it.
1445945.flag: Escalante's 1776 route predates the Old Spanish Trail; check wording.

1445992.name: Spring City
1445992.original: Vacated 1853, resettled 1859. So named because of the springs on the settlement site.
1445992.rewrite: Settlers left in 1853 and returned in 1859. Named for the springs on the settlement site.

1446051.name: Spring Lake
1446051.original: So named because of a near-by small lake formed by several springs. Known as Spring Lake Villa prior to 1862.
1446051.rewrite: Named for a small nearby lake formed by several springs. Known as Spring Lake Villa before 1862.

1446057.name: Springville
1446057.original: So named because of a large spring near the townsite. First called Hobble Creek for a near-by stream which was so named by a group of traders who, while camped near the creek, lost a pair of hobbles from their bell horse.
1446057.rewrite: Named for a large spring near the townsite. First called Hobble Creek for a nearby stream, named by a group of traders who lost a pair of hobbles from their bell horse while camped near the creek.

1446134.name: Sterling
1446134.original: Origin of present name unknown. First named Pettyville for the Petty family, early settlers. Later called Leesburg, Buncetown, and Pettytown.
1446134.rewrite: Origin of present name unknown. First named Pettyville for the Petty family, early settlers. Later called Leesburg, Buncetown and Pettytown.

1446361.name: Teasdale
1446361.original: Named for George Teasdale, Mormon Church official and early pioneer.
1446361.rewrite: Named for George Teasdale, a leader in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and an early pioneer.

1446533.name: Thistle
1446533.original: So named because of the prolific growth of wild thistles in this region.
1446533.rewrite: Named for the abundant wild thistles in the region.

1446655.name: Toquerville
1446655.original: Named for Chief Toquer. Toquer is a Ute Indian word meaning "black."
1446655.rewrite: Named for Toquer, a Native American leader. Toquer is a Ute word meaning "black."
1446655.flag: Toquer is often described as a Paiute leader; check whether the word is Ute or Paiute.

1446658.name: Torrey
1446658.original: Named in honor of Colonel Torrey of Wyoming, who fought in the Spanish-American War. First called Poverty Flat.
1446658.rewrite: Named in honor of Col. Torrey of Wyoming, who fought in the Spanish-American War. First called Poverty Flat.
1446658.flag: Col. Jay L. Torrey's regiment reportedly never saw combat; check "fought."

1446722.name: Tropic
1446722.original: So named because of its warm climate as compared to that of Panguitch from which its first settlers came.
1446722.rewrite: Named for its warm climate compared with that of Panguitch, where its first settlers came from.

1446835.name: Uintah
1446835.original: Named for a Ute Indian tribe. First called East Weber, and later, Easton, because it was settled on the east bank of the Weber River. At first the railroad called the local station Deseret, but later changed the name to Uintah, and the town subsequently adopted the same name.
1446835.rewrite: Named for a Ute tribe. First called East Weber, and later Easton, because it was settled on the east bank of the Weber River. The railroad at first called the local station Deseret but later changed the name to Uintah, and the town then adopted the same name.

1446921.name: Venice
1446921.original: Outgrowth of Glenwood. Named for Venice, Italy. First called Wallsville in honor of William Wall, early settler.
1446921.rewrite: An outgrowth of Glenwood. Named for Venice, Italy. First called Wallsville in honor of William Wall, an early settler.

1446932.name: Vernon
1446932.original: Named for Joseph Vernon, early settler, who was killed by Indians.
1446932.rewrite: Named for Joseph Vernon, an early settler said to have been killed by Native Americans.
1446932.flag: Killing not confirmed in other sources; hedged with "said to have been."

1446936.name: Veyo
1446936.original: Name coined from the words "verdure" and "youth" by a group of Mormon Beehive Girls.
1446936.rewrite: Name coined from the words "verdure" and "youth" by a group of Latter-day Saint Beehive Girls.

1446954.name: Wales
1446954.original: Named for the British principality. Formerly called Coalville because of the early discovery of coal in this vicinity.
1446954.rewrite: Named for the British principality. Formerly called Coalville because of the early discovery of coal in the area.

1446968.name: Wallsburg
1446968.original: Named for William W. Wall, early settler.
1446968.rewrite: Named for William W. Wall, an early settler.

1446995.name: Warren
1446995.original: Named for Lewis Warren Shurtliff, early settler. First known as Salt Creek.
1446995.rewrite: Named for Lewis Warren Shurtliff, an early settler. First known as Salt Creek.

1447016.name: Washakie
1447016.original: Named for a Shoshone leader who was friendly to the early settlers of northern Utah.
1447016.rewrite: Named for a Shoshone leader who was friendly with the early settlers of northern Utah.

1447019.name: Washington
1447019.original: Named in honor of George Washington, first President of the United States.
1447019.rewrite: Named in honor of George Washington, first president of the United States.

1447103.name: Wellsville
1447103.original: Named for Daniel H. Wells, pioneer settler.
1447103.rewrite: Named for Daniel H. Wells, a pioneer settler.

1447187.name: West Weber
1447187.original: So named to distinguish it from East Weber and South Weber, near-by settlements. Composed of the older settlements of Alma, Weston, Taylorsville and Garland.
1447187.rewrite: Named to distinguish it from East Weber and South Weber, nearby settlements. Made up of the older settlements of Alma, Weston, Taylorsville and Garland.

1447328.name: Widtsoe
1447328.original: Vacated. Named in honor of John A. Widtsoe, Mormon Church official and former president of the University of Utah. First called Windor, and later Houston.
1447328.rewrite: Vacated. Named in honor of John A. Widtsoe, a leader in The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints and former president of the University of Utah. First called Windor, and later Houston.

1447372.name: Willard
1447372.original: Named for Willard Richards, counselor to Brigham Young. First called North Willow Creek, taking the early name of the stream near which the first settlement was made.
1447372.rewrite: Named for Willard Richards, counselor to Brigham Young. First called North Willow Creek, the early name of the stream near which the first settlement was made.

1447521.name: Woods Cross
1447521.original: Derived its name from a railroad crossing near the farm of Daniel C. Wood. From Woods Crossing, the name was shortened to Woods Cross.
1447521.rewrite: Named for a railroad crossing near the farm of Daniel C. Wood. The name was shortened from Woods Crossing to Woods Cross.

1449150.name: Vineyard
1449150.original: Outgrowth of Lakeview. So named because early settlers devoted many acres to the raising of grapes.
1449150.rewrite: An outgrowth of Lakeview. Named for the many acres early settlers devoted to growing grapes.

1450429.name: Mendon
1450429.original: Named for Mendon, Worcester County, Massachusetts, birthplace of Ezra T. Benson, first Mormon apostle to live in Cache Valley.
1450429.rewrite: Named for Mendon, Worcester County, Massachusetts, birthplace of Ezra T. Benson, the first Latter-day Saint apostle to live in Cache Valley.

1451119.name: Mammoth
1451119.original: Received its name in 1870 following the discovery of rich ore in the Mammoth mine in the near-by mountains.
1451119.rewrite: Named in 1870 after the discovery of rich ore in the Mammoth mine in the nearby mountains.

1454595.name: Flowell
1454595.original: So named because of a large number of flowing wells in the town. The local church and most of the homes are constructed of black volcanic rock. First known as Crystal.
1454595.rewrite: Named for the many flowing wells in the town. The local church and most of the homes were built of black volcanic rock. First known as Crystal.

1454997.name: Salt Lake City
1454997.original: Derived its name from Great Salt Lake, which was so named because of the extreme salinity of its water. Until 1868 the settlement was called Great Salt Lake City.
1454997.rewrite: Named for Great Salt Lake, which was named for the extreme salinity of its water. The settlement was called Great Salt Lake City until 1868.

1455092.name: Deweyville
1455092.original: Named for John C. Dewey, one of its first settlers.
1455092.rewrite: Named for John C. Dewey, one of its first settlers.

1455096.name: Milton
1455096.original: So named because of a grist mill built here in 1864 by George W. Taggart and the Hinman brothers.
1455096.rewrite: Named for a gristmill built here in 1864 by George W. Taggart and the Hinman brothers.

1455098.name: St. George
1455098.original: Named for George A. Smith, counselor to Brigham Young.
1455098.rewrite: Named for George A. Smith, counselor to Brigham Young.

1455150.name: Perry
1455150.original: Named for the Perry family, early settlers. First called Porter Springs for Orin Porter Rockwell, early land owner. Later called Three-Mile Creek because it is near a stream three miles south of Brigham City.
1455150.rewrite: Named for the Perry family, early settlers. First called Porter Springs for Orrin Porter Rockwell, an early landowner. Later called Three-Mile Creek because it is near a stream three miles south of Brigham City.
1455150.flag: Book spells it Orin; corrected to Orrin.

1455878.name: Heber
1455878.original: Named for Heber C. Kimball, early pioneer and counselor to Brigham Young.
1455878.rewrite: Named for Heber C. Kimball, an early pioneer and counselor to Brigham Young.

1455905.name: Sandy
1455905.original: So named because of the sandy nature of the soil.

1681817.name: Portage
1681817.original: Named for Portage County, Ohio, birthplace of Lorenzo Snow, fifth president of the Mormon Church. Formerly called Hay Town because of the large fields of hay grown by the early settlers.
1681817.rewrite: Named for Portage County, Ohio, birthplace of Lorenzo Snow, fifth president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. Formerly called Hay Town because of the large fields of hay grown by the early settlers.

1867579.name: Millcreek
1867579.original: Derived its name from the stream on which it is situated.
1867579.rewrite: Named for the stream on which it sits.

2408067.name: Elberta
2408067.original: Formerly called Mount Nebo for a near-by mountain peak. In 1905 it was changed to Elberta because many orchards of Elberta peaches were planted here.
2408067.rewrite: Formerly called Mount Nebo for a nearby mountain peak. The name was changed to Elberta in 1905 because many orchards of Elberta peaches were planted here.

UGRC-beaver-dam-box-elder.name: Beaver Dam
UGRC-beaver-dam-box-elder.original: So named because of the beaver dams along the stream near which the settlement was established.
UGRC-beaver-dam-box-elder.rewrite: Named for the beaver dams along the stream near which the settlement was established.

UGRC-cove-fort-millard.name: Cove Fort
UGRC-cove-fort-millard.original: Built during the Indian wars of the 1860's. Believed to have received its name because of the protection and shelter of the surrounding mountains.
UGRC-cove-fort-millard.rewrite: Built during conflicts with Native Americans in the 1860s. Believed to have been named for the protection and shelter of the surrounding mountains.

UGRC-iosepa-tooele.name: Iosepa
UGRC-iosepa-tooele.original: Named for a group of Mormon converts from the Hawaiian Islands who attempted to establish a settlement here. Iosepa is Hawaiian for "Joseph" and was selected as a name in honor of Joseph F. Smith, who served several missions to the islands and who later became president of the Mormon Church.
UGRC-iosepa-tooele.rewrite: Named for a group of Latter-day Saint converts from the Hawaiian Islands who tried to establish a settlement here. Iosepa is Hawaiian for "Joseph" and was chosen in honor of Joseph F. Smith, who served several missions to the islands and later became president of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

UGRC-pinto-washington.name: Pinto
UGRC-pinto-washington.original: Spanish word for "painted" or "mottled." So named because of the vari-colored geologic formations around the area.
UGRC-pinto-washington.rewrite: Spanish word for "painted" or "mottled." Named for the multicolored geologic formations in the area.

UGRC-promontory-point-box-elder.name: Promontory Point
UGRC-promontory-point-box-elder.original: So named because it is situated on the point of the promontory projecting into the north end of Great Salt Lake.
UGRC-promontory-point-box-elder.rewrite: Named for its location on the point of the promontory projecting into the north end of Great Salt Lake.

UGRC-tintic-juab.name: Tintic
UGRC-tintic-juab.rewrite: Named for a Native American leader.

UGRC-west-warren-weber.name: West Warren
UGRC-west-warren-weber.original: Outgrowth of Warren. So named because it is west of the older settlement.
UGRC-west-warren-weber.rewrite: An outgrowth of Warren. Named for its location west of the older settlement.

UGRC-woodrow-millard.name: Woodrow
UGRC-woodrow-millard.original: Named in honor of Woodrow Wilson, twenty-seventh President of the United States.
UGRC-woodrow-millard.flag: Book calls Wilson the 27th president (he was the 28th); number dropped.
